  COVID-19 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION OPTIONS
Due to the existing COVID-19 health emergency and the social distancing measures currently in effect, and pursuant
to Assembly Bill 361, please note that members of the public will be allowed only to observe and address the City
Council Meeting of Tuesday, March 1, 2022, at 2:00 p.m. (or 1:00 p.m. if Closed Session) by telephone, video
and other electronic means, as follows:

  1. Written Public Comments: Members of the public may choose to submit comments electronically for
  consideration by the Inglewood City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/Finance Authority/Parking
  Authority/Joint Powers Authority (Legislative Body) by sending them to the City Clerk/Secretary at
  athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To ensure
  distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
  comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
  number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments
  received after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public
  record of the meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  March 1, 2022

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  March 1, 2022, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance
  Authority, Parking Authority, and Joint Powers at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary/Parking Authority Secretary/Joint Powers Authority Secretary
  announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/
  Finance Authority Chairman/ Parking Authority Chairman/ Joint
  Powers Authority Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor
  Agency Members/Housing Authority Members/ Finance Authority
  Members/ Parking Authority Members/Joint Powers Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.

  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority/ Finance Authority/ Parking Authority/ Joint
  Powers officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, Housing Authority, Finance Authority,
  Parking Authority, and Joint Powers Authority.

  Mayor Butts announced that Agenda Item No. DR-3 has been pulled from the Agenda.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman/Parking Authority
  Chairman/Joint Powers Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons
  present who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing
  Authority/Finance Authority/Parking Authority/Joint Powers Authority on any item on
  the Agendas, other than the public hearings.

  City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported public comments received via email, and
  distributed to the Mayor and City Council.

  Caller (Name Unknown) commented on Agenda Item Nos. 8, Payment of Invoice No.
  100006 to LAZ Parking, for Shuttle services provided for the Taste of Inglewood Big
  Game Concert Series Festival Event, and DR-1, Fiscal Year 2021-2022 First-Quarter
  Budget Review Report.

  Caller (Name Unkown) commented on the Taste of Inglewood, a reward for the shooting
  that took place in Inglewood, and Agenda Item No. PH-1, Public Hearing to approve
  draft maps, and receive and file public comments.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated
  February 25, 2022, in the amount of $3,629,390.17, and February 17, 2022, in the amount
  of $4,729,615.02  are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency
  Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers

  1
   March 1, 2022

  that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

126  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – APPROVAL OF DRAFT MAPS; RECEIVE AND
  FILE PUBLIC COMMENTS. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled matter
  was a public hearing to consider, discuss, and draw Draft Council District Maps, Council
  District Boundaries, and Communities of Interest, and receive and file public comments
  in accordance with the Fair Maps Act, and that notice was given in the time, form and
  manner as required by law, and communications were received.

  The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson received communications via email from Maggie
  Ikemi, who requested that the section of District 1 North of Florence Avenue be re-
  assigned to District 2, and Amy A. Ulloa, who wanted to discuss why District 1 has the
  streets north of Florence as well as Edward Vincent Park.

  Mayor Butts ordered the communications received and filed.

  Artie Fields, City Manager, presented the staff report dated March 1, 2022.

  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk gave a brief oral report regarding the redistricting
  purpose and process.

  Mayor Butts left the dais at 2:16 p.m.

  Elsa Moreno, GIS Analyst, Public Works Department, presented an overview on how to
  locate the interactive mapping tool and how it is used to create draft maps. She also
  demonstrated how to access the mapping template.

  Mayor Butts returned to the dais at 2:17 p.m.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  Fredrisha Dixon, spoke regarding the City Council meeting not being broadcasted.

  Margarete (Last Name Unknown), objected to the current draft maps, and requested that
  the maps be redrawn like they were in 2016.

  Mayor Butts closed public comments at the hour of 2:24 p.m.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council does hereby approve the draft maps. The motion was carried by the following
  roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public comments received and filed.

131.8  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – REVISED 2020 CONSOLIDATED ANNUAL
  PERFORMANCE EVALUTION REPORT (CAPER) FOR FISCAL YEAR 2020-
  2021 TO THE U.S. DEPARTMENT OF HOUSING AND URBAN
  DEVELOPMENT. Staff report dated March 1, 2022, was presented to conduct a public
  hearing to consider approval of the proposed Revised 2020 Consolidated Annual
  Performance Evaluation Report (CAPER) for Fiscal Year 2020-2021 to the U.S.
  Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing continued to the Council Meeting of March 8,
  2022, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  2
   March 1, 2022

  MINUTES. It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council
  Member Morales that the Minutes for the City Council Meetings held on February 2,
  2022 (Special), February 8, 2022, and February 15, 2022, be approved. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. Cinette Cowart for alleged personal injury; broken utility lid in sidewalk on May 8,
  2021.
  2. Jaime Hernandez for alleged tire damage; pothole on January 10, 2022.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby reject claims listed as A-1 and A-2. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 21-148 APPROVED – CSG
  CONSULTANTS, INC., INTERWEST CONSULTING GROUP, INC., AND J LEE
  ENGINEERING, INC. Staff report dated March 1, 2022, was presented recommending
  approval of the second amendment to Agreement No. 21-148, for Building Plan Check
  consulting services.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby approve second amendment to Agreement No. 21-148,
  in an additional amount not to exceed $500,000 (total amount not to exceed $1,075,000)
  with the following consultants: 1) CSG Consultants, Inc.; 2) Interwest Consulting Group,
  Inc.; and 3) J Lee Engineering, Inc. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PURCHASE ORDER AUTHORIZED – MERIDIAN RAPID DEFENSE GROUP
  (MERIDIAN). Staff report dated March 1, 2022, was presented recommending
  authorization of issuance of a purchase order to Meridian Rapid Defense Group
  (Meridian), for the purchase of Anti-Vehicle Barriers and Accessories, per Bid No. RFB-
  0146.

  It was moved by Council Member Dotson, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that the City Council does hereby authorize issuance in the amount of $186,901.45. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  AGREEMENT NO. 22-155 APPROVED – HNTB CORPORATION; MAYOR

  TRANSIT CONNECTOR PROJECT; RESOLUTION NO. 22-56 ADOPTED –
  AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2021-2022 ANNUAL BUDGET. Staff report

 183  PUBLIC HEARING SET – CONSIDER AN ORDINANCE AMENDING
  CHAPTER 2 (ADMINISTRATION), ARTICLE 5 (PURCHASING), SECTION 2-
  201; CHAPTER 5 (OFFENSES, MISCELLANEOUS), ARTICLE 7 (WATER
  CONSERVATION), SECTION 5-112.1 (WATER EFFICIENCY IN THE
  LANDSCAPE); AND CHAPTER 7 (SANITATION AND HEALTH
  REGULATIONS), ARTICLE 7 (CONSTRUCTION AND DEMOLITION
  RECYCLING PROGRAM), SECTION 7-79 OF THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE (IMC) IN COMPLIANCE WITH CALIFORNIA SENATE BILL 1383.
  Staff report dated March 1, 2022, was presented requesting that a public hearing be set to
  consider an ordinance amending Chapter 2 (Administration), Article 5 (Purchasing),
  Section 2-201; Chapter 5 (Offenses, Miscellaneous), Article 7 (Water Conservation),
  Section 5-112.1 (Water Efficiency in the Landscape); and Chapter 7 (Sanitation and
  Health Regulations), Article 7 (Construction and Demolition Recycling Program),
  Section 7-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code (IMC), to update organic waste recycling
  requirements for residents and businesses in compliance with California Senate Bill 1383.

  Mayor Butts set the public hearing for March 22, 2022, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. The City Clerk, Aisha L. Thompson, reported on March
  marking the celebration of National Women’s History Month, and the theme being
  “Women Providing Healing, Promoting Hope.” She stated the theme is a tribute to the
  ongoing work of caregivers and frontline workers. She also paid homage to Ketanji
  Brown Jackson, for being the first black woman nominated to the U.S. Supreme Court
  Justice. Finally, she reminded residents of the online redistricting mapping tool located
  on the City’s website, and all draft maps are due on March 10, 2022, by 10:00 a.m.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Caller (Name Unknown) spoke concerning the opening of the Community Room for in-
  person participation at the City Council meetings.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in memory of Eleanor Wallace, a Teacher for Inglewood Unified School
  District, at the hour of 3:06 p.m.
